segments.text: The theory of relativity, proposed by Albert Einstein, fundamentally changed our understanding of space and time. Its two main components, special relativity and general relativity, address the behavior of objects in motion and the influence of gravity on the fabric of spacetime. Special relativity introduced the concept of time dilation, where time appears to pass more slowly for objects moving at high speeds. This led to the realization that simultaneity is relative, depending on the observer's frame of reference. General relativity expanded on this idea, describing gravity not as a force but as a curvature of spacetime caused by mass. This innovative perspective has been confirmed through numerous experiments and is essential for the accurate functioning of technologies like GPS.

academic.passage: Albert Einstein's theory of relativity revolutionized the field of physics by introducing new concepts about space and time. It includes two major parts: special relativity, which focuses on objects moving at constant speeds, and general relativity, which explains how gravity affects the structure of spacetime. Special relativity reveals that time can vary for moving observers, while general relativity describes gravity as a result of the curvature of spacetime caused by mass. These theories have had profound implications for both theoretical and applied physics, influencing technologies such as satellite navigation.
